subject: Mary of Egypt
note: One writer, research and writing in one pass (SAINT-BRIEF.md). Every fetched text is under design/saints-hub/sources/people/mary-of-egypt/ (gitignored). No public-domain English translation of the whole Greek Life was found; the page quotes the Old English Life (from Paul the Deacon of Naples's Latin) in the translation of W. W. Skeat's EETS edition (Skeat with Miss Gunning and Miss Wilkinson), and the Greek passage John of Damascus quoted, tr. Mary H. Allies (1898). The OCA's life (a modern retelling of the Greek) was read for facts (1 April, the icon above her, Zosimas nearly a hundred) but never quoted as her words. Helen Waddell and Maria Kouli's translation are not quoted; Kouli's own introduction (her words as a scholar) is. Skeat's bracketed passages are his supplements from the Latin where the Old English is lost; the page quotes two lines from inside one (the blush and the adder), which are still the edition's translation. Zero-width spaces were stripped from the fetched Wikisource texts so the script can match across page joins.

life.text: Left home and a brother in Egypt at twelve for Alexandria; seventeen years of lust; took no money; lived in poverty; spun flax (the flax-stick she threw away).
life.source: The Life, tr. in Skeat's edition

life.text: Aged 29 when she joined the pilgrims; the Exaltation of the Cross is 14 September; Sophronius patriarch 634 to 638; authorship debated (Zonaras and Delehaye for; Halkin and Beck against); probably 600s since John of Damascus cited it; earliest version in Cyril of Scythopolis's Life of Kyriakos (a singer at the church of the Resurrection, eighteen years on a jar of water and a basket of legumes, buried by the monk John); Moschos's similar tale; 'impossible ... to establish her historicity'; the lion echoes Jerome's Life of Paul; about a third of the Life is her first-person account; versions in Syriac, Armenian, Ethiopic, Slavonic; 27 Greek manuscripts in Athens, 37 in Paris; Byzantine art shows her thin, dark, in Zosimas's cloak, often with him.
life.source: Maria Kouli, introduction, Holy Women of Byzantium (Dumbarton Oaks, 1996)

life.text: Born probably about 344; died about 421; Bollandists: died 1 April 421, many others a century later; Life written before 500 by another hand (Bollandists); written by one who learned it from Zosimas's monks; 'public prostitution'; a statue of the Virgin above her; aided by a lion; relics at Rome, Naples, Cremona, Antwerp; Greek feast 1 April, Roman Martyrology 2 April, Roman Calendar 3 April, perhaps the days her relics reached the West.
Coptic synaxarium 6 Baramouda: departed 421, born in Alexandria about 345 of Christian parents, the lion, lived 76 years.

Zosimas's monastery on the Jordan and its Lenten rule; he saw her dark from the sun, hair white as wool; she named him and knew he was a priest; raised 'the space of a man's ell' as she prayed; 47 years in the desert; 2 1/2 loaves that lasted seventeen years; seventeen years of temptation; never learned to read; she smiled; Holy Thursday communion, walked on the Jordan by moonlight, Nunc dimittis, three lentils; message to Abbot John; found dead facing east a year later, writing on the ground, twenty days' journey in an hour, the lion dug the grave, buried in the torn cloak; the monks kept the day of her death.
life.source: The Life, tr. in Skeat's edition

life.text: Golden Legend: 'refused no man'; loaves 'sufficed to me seventeen years'; raised 'well nigh a foot and a half'; the lion. Magdalene chapter: thirty years in a desert near Aix, lifted by angels, raised 'the space of two or three cubits', last communion from Bishop Maximin.
life.source: The Golden Legend, tr. Caxton, ed. Ellis (1900)

life.text: John of Damascus, On Holy Images, quotes her prayer before the image of the Mother of God and her thanks after; his own line on the 'statue'.
life.source: John of Damascus, On Holy Images, tr. Mary H. Allies (1898)

life.text: Jerome's Life of Paul: Antony had no implement for digging; two lions dug the grave.
life.source: Jerome, Life of Paulus the First Hermit, NPNF2 vol. 6 (1893)

life.text: Goethe's Maria Aegyptiaca speech in the last scene of Faust Part Two, with Magna Peccatrix and Mulier Samaritana, before the Mater Gloriosa.
An ancient temple on the north side of the Piazza della Bocca della Verita was converted into the church of S. Maria Egiziaca in 872.

The Standing of St Mary of Egypt: Thursday Matins of the fifth week (usually served Wednesday evening); the Great Canon and her Life read in full, the Life in two parts; called the Standing because the canon is heard standing; the only one of the Typikon's hagiographies still read in parishes.
The Great Canon is sung whole on Thursday of the fifth week; Andrew made bishop in Crete under Justinian II (685 to 695).
life.source: OCA, Saint Andrew, Archbishop of Crete

life.text: OCA life: Zosimas's day 4 April; the icon above her; the writing gave 1 April; Zosimas lived to nearly a hundred. Read for facts only (a modern retelling).
Episcopal Church: 3 April, 'Mary of Egypt, Monastic, c. 421'; 'an Alexandrian prostitute'; most of what is known is based on the Life; the collect.

The 1648 icon: Yakov Kazanets, spring 1648, painted for the wedding of Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich and Tsaritsa Maria Ilyinichna (Miloslavskaya); tempera on wood, 48 x 58.5 cm, inv. Zh-166 (the Commons file's description, from icon-art.ru).

feasts.who: Catholic, Martyrologium Romanum (2004), 1 April, entry 3: 'In Palaestina, sanctae Mariae Aegyptiacae, quae, celebris peccatrix alexandrina, ad Deum in Civitate Sancta, beata Virgine intercedente, conversa trans Iordanem paenitentem vitam solitaria duxit.' Index: 'Maria Aegyptia, 1 apr., 3 (s. V)'.
Roman Martyrology 1916, end of 2 April: 'In Palestine, the decease of St. Mary of Egypt, surnamed the Sinner.' Index: 'Sinner' Apr. 2.
Episcopal Church, Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022; the old Roman Calendar (Catholic Encyclopedia)
OCA (new calendar), Venerable Mary of Egypt
Old-calendar churches (1 April Julian); Coptic 6 Baramouda (Baramouda 1 is 9 April Gregorian and 27 March Julian, so 6 Baramouda is 14 April, the old 1 April)

feasts.date: Fifth Sunday of Great Lent (18 April 2027)
feasts.who: OCA lists 18 April 2027 as the 5th Sunday of Great Lent: St Mary of Egypt (Orthodox Pascha 2 May 2027)
Not in the Church of England calendar or the LCMS and ELCA lists on disk; not in the USCCB 2026 or 1969 general Roman calendar

pictures.rejected: Every Eastern icon found (Mstera 19th c., Kirillo-Belozersk, the 1804 icon with 16 scenes, a 17th-c. hagiographic icon, a 19th-c. icon with a 1939.ru watermark, the Serbian-school Communion of 1723 at the Petit Palais) shows her torso bare under the cloak. Ribera 1641 (Prado and Montpellier), Franceschini (Met), Czechowicz, Trevisani, Vaccaro, Massys, Lorenzo di Credi and Marianna Elmo's embroidery: bare or hair-covered. Tintoretto (San Rocco): her face is not seen. 'Ikone Maria Aegyptiaca Zosimas' is tagged copyrighted free use, not PD or CC0.

could_not_verify: No public-domain English translation of the Greek Life was found (the modern ones, Waddell 1936 and Kouli 1996, are in copyright). Mahler's use of Goethe's Maria Aegyptiaca in his Eighth Symphony and the reading of the Life at the Second Council of Nicaea (787) were not checked in a fetched source and are left out. The date of Luca Giordano's Ghent picture is not on its Commons page; the caption gives none. Jerome's Life of Paul is dated only 'in the 300s' on the page.

checked: Numbers against Skeat's text: twelve and seventeen years ('in the twelfth year of my age'; 'for seventeen years'), 'seven and forty years', 'two and a half loaves ... hardened, like stone' and 'For seventeen years ... I made use of the loaves', the twenty days' journey fulfilled 'in the course of an hour'; 29 at the voyage and the Exaltation on 14 September (Kouli); 'perhaps one-third of the whole' (Kouli); 27 Greek manuscripts in Athens and 37 in the Bibliotheque Nationale (Kouli); 872 and the temple on the Piazza della Bocca della Verita (Platner and Ashby); Coptic 6 Baramouda: 421, born about 345, 'seventy six years'.

Feasts: 1 April in the 2004 Martyrologium (entry read in mr2004.txt), 2 April in the 1916 Martyrology ('surnamed the Sinner'), 3 April in LFF 2022 and the old Roman Calendar (CE); 1 April OCA; 14 April old calendar and Coptic 6 Baramouda; the fifth Sunday of Lent on 18 April 2027 (OCA). CE: 'the others may be due to the fact that on those days portions of her relics reached the West.'

Attributions and disputes: CE (MacRory 1910) on 344 and 421, the Bollandists' 1 April 421 and 'a century later', 'written before 500', relics at Rome, Naples, Cremona, Antwerp; Kouli on Cyril of Scythopolis (a singer, eighteen years on water and legumes, buried by the monk John), Moschos, Zonaras and Delehaye for Sophronius, Halkin and Beck against; Jerome's two lions; John of Damascus's 'statue'; LFF's 'Alexandrian prostitute' and 'self-emptying' in their context; the Golden Legend's 'refused no man' and Magdalene's thirty years.

Scenes against Skeat: a brother and a home in Egypt; no money taken; the young man who 'departed from me, laughing'; three pence and three loaves; the corner of the vestibule; 'Ah, thou spiritual mother' (the path's 'Mother'); levitation sworn 'taking God as a witness'; the moonlit crossing; figs, dates and three lentils; abbot John amended the customs; hands laid and 'turned eastwards'; the lioness gone 'like the gentlest lamb'.

Rules: capitals for God in every quotation (the Nunc dimittis and Zosimas's blessing capitalised; 'thy Son' and 'thy goodness' rightly lower case, addressed to the Mother of God); no section marks; italicize.mjs dry run reports nothing; seo title 63 and description 153 characters; the 'Who' answer 53 words; tiles read on their own, none a slight.

changed: Trait 'humble before a priest': Skeat has Zosimas 'endeavouring to bend his knees' and her crying 'from the waters and to forbid him'. 'Zosimas knelt to her. She stopped him from the river' became 'Zosimas tried to kneel to her. She called from the river to stop him'.
Circle, the Mother of God: 'chose her as her guarantor' became 'protector', the edition's word ('choose thee for my protector').
Circle, Andrew of Crete: the OCA says he was made bishop in Crete under Justinian II (685 to 695), so 'from the 690s' became 'from the late 600s'.
How she died: Skeat buries her 'as naked as when he first saw her, except for ... the torn strip which Zosimus formerly threw to her'; 'in the torn cloak' became 'with only the torn piece of cloak'.
'Who wrote it': Kouli says the Life 'was probably composed in the seventh century'; 'dates it to the 600s' became 'thinks it was probably written in the 600s'.
'Is she a saint?': 'Her honour began with the monks who first heard her story' told the Life as history in our voice; now 'In the *Life*, her honour begins with the monks ... It grew from there.'
for_owner: Luca Giordano's portrait: a low neckline and, as usual, an unclothed Christ Child; the scene is dark and her face is middling in size.
The Chasseriau/Haussoullier engraving is black and white and has a small putto in the crowd scene.
The prostitute myth sets the CE's and the Episcopal Church's word against her own 'not for money', with the Golden Legend's 'refused no man': plain but decent, his call.
Band and card lede 'The runaway of Alexandria': she ran away TO Alexandria from elsewhere in Egypt; left as written (it reads as where she lived).
